newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian trade won't open up until industry better.
newsitem.headline: Russian trade won't open up until industry better.

text.p: Russia will not open up its markets further to foreign trade until the state of its own industry improves, Prime-Tass news agency quoted Foreign Trade Minister Oleg Davydov as saying on Friday.
"For the time being, we cannot move towards further opening our own markets," Davydov, who is also a deputy prime minister, said in the Urals industrial city of Yekaterinburg.
Davydov said that it would take five to six years until Russian industry could compete properly with the West as it undergoes structural change.
"Then we will lower trade barriers, and improve conditions for access to the Russian market for importers," he said.
Davydov was quoted as saying that Russia would support its own market in the same way that other countries, including the European Union, raise barriers to Russian suppliers.
His protectionist rhetoric is part of a growing chorus by Russian officials who have urged measures to support ailing domestic industry.
But Russia has sometimes backed down from blocking foreign access to its markets.
